question: Tang vs. Markelov: Match O/U 23.5
description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Sheng Tang and Artem Markelov in the M25 Guiyang, originally scheduled for September 14, 2026 at 10:00PM ET.
This market will resolve to "Over" if the total number of games completed equals or exceeds 24. Otherwise, it will resolve to "Under." All tiebreaks, including any Champions/Super tiebreak, count as one (1) game.
If the match is postponed or suspended, this market will remain open until the match has been completed. A postponement alone will not trigger a 50-50 resolution.
If the match is permanently abandoned before completion, or if the match has not been completed by September 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve 50-50, unless the outcome has already been unconditionally determined based on completed play. An outcome is considered determined if it would have been guaranteed had the match been played to completion using the minimum number of additional games required. For example, for a line of 21.5, if play stops at 6-3, 5-6, completing the match would have required at least 2 additional games, resulting in at least 22 games played, so "Over" would resolve as the winning outcome.
The primary resolution source for this market will be official ITF statistics; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: M25 Guiyang: Sheng Tang vs Artem Markelov
events.description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Sheng Tang and Artem Markelov in the M25 Guiyang, Qualifying, originally scheduled for September 14, 2026 at 10:00PM ET.

This market will resolve to 'Sheng Tang' if Sheng Tang advances against Artem Markelov.

This market will resolve to 'Artem Markelov' if Artem Markelov advances against Sheng Tang.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or a winner has not been determined by September 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (14 days after the scheduled start), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one player advances due to the opponent's retirement, default, or disqualification, this market will resolve to the player who advances.

If the match ends in a walkover (player withdraws before the start and the other advances automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the International Tennis Federation (ITF). A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
